RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-women panel is not evidence of anything on its own. Panels in clinical laboratory medicine and HR are often female-majority simply because the field is; composition tells you nothing about how any individual decision was made. Raising it as your opening argument makes you look like you're explaining away a loss, and it undermines the parts of your case that are actually solid.

What is solid: you hold a PhD and she a master's, and the employer has ignored a reasonable request for two weeks. Chase the written explanation in writing, citing any statutory deadline. Ask specifically how formal qualifications and "broad leadership experience" were weighted and scored. If the reasoning turns out to be vague or shifting, that is worth pursuing — on its own merits.
